html:
The Monacan are a Siouan-speaking people of the Virginia Piedmont, upstream of the falls of the James River. The English at Jamestown heard of them in 1607 as enemies of the Powhatan chiefdom of the coastal plain. They had towns on the upper James and built earth burial mounds.

Disease and settlers scattered them in the 1700s; some joined the Tutelo and Saponi and moved north to the Haudenosaunee. Others stayed around Bear Mountain in Amherst County, where an Episcopal mission school served them from 1908. Under Virginia's race laws of the 1920s officials listed them as "colored", denying them an Indian identity. The Monacan Indian Nation won federal recognition in 2018.
